newsitem.title: UK: NatWest sees options loss report in a month.
newsitem.headline: NatWest sees options loss report in a month.

text.p: A report into a 90 million stg loss on interest rate options trading at NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank Plc, is expected to be complete in around a month, NatWest chairman Lord Alexander said on Tuesday.
Alexander was replying to a question at the bank's annual meeting.
He said the report, being compiled by accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand and law firm Linklaters & Paines, would give recommendations as to how such a loss could be avoided in future.
"I expect the report in about a month but please don't hold me to that," Alexander said.
Earlier, Alexander had said that NatWest would publish as much of the report as possible but might be constrained by commercial and legal considerations.

Questioned on the role of NatWest's auditors KPMG, Alexander refused to comment, saying that this was an aspect that the report would be concerned with and that it would be wrong to pre-judge its conclusions.
KPMG was reappointed as auditor of the firm at least until the next AGM.
The loss will translate into a 77 million stg loss in NatWest's first half accounts after provisions and bonus cuts are taken into account.
Neil Dodgson, global head of options at NatWest Markets has been suspended since the loss came to light in February. It later suspended four other executives.
Kyriacos Papouis, the options trader alleged to be at the centre of the loss, has left NatWest Markets and also left his subsequent employer Bear Stearns.
